articles.title: Pittsburgh Steelers vs Cleveland Browns Week 8: Steel Rolls 27-6
articles.matchup: Final: Cleveland Browns (5-3) 6, Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) 27, Sun., Nov. 1, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: bye week, then at Cincinnati Bengals, Sun., Nov. 15, 8:20 PM ET, Paycor Stadium, Cincinnati
articles.text:
Pittsburgh Steelers 27, Cleveland Browns 6. Sunday afternoon, along the Mon, the old Carrie Blast Furnaces lit up for Samhain, a fire festival running from 3 to 9 PM inside the old mill. Down at Acrisure Stadium, another old Pittsburgh furnace was running hot. That made 23 straight regular-season home wins over Cleveland, tying the NFL record.

It started like it always does against these guys. Cleveland went backward. Daylen Everette ripped the ball from Harold Fannin Jr. on the opening drive, and Pittsburgh won the challenge to get it. Chris Boswell missed from 57, so Patrick Queen and Cameron Heyward went and got it back, splitting a sack of Deshaun Watson as Queen jarred the ball loose and Keeanu Benton fell on it. Five plays later, Rico Dowdle ran 9 yards for a 7-0 lead. The Browns finished the first quarter with minus-1 yard.

Jaylen Warren set the tone on a third-and-13, bursting 51 yards up the middle, and Boswell added two field goals. Andre Szmyt kept Cleveland close with kicks from 32 and 49, and it was 13-6 with 45 seconds left in the half. Then Warren went 23 yards, Pat Freiermuth caught one for 28, Germie Bernard got us to the 1, and with no timeouts left Mike McCarthy skipped the chip shot. Direct snap to Freiermuth, touchdown, 20-6 with one second showing.

Early in the third, Heyward blew up Quinshon Judkins on a third-and-1. Next time we had it, Aaron Rodgers found Darnell Washington for 58 yards to the 1, and Warren punched it in for 27-6. Warren finished with 143 yards on 17 carries. Washington had a career-high 94 on three catches.

The defense did the rest. Eight sacks, the most since 2021. T.J. Watt had two, giving him 20.5 against Cleveland, the most by any player against the Browns in NFL history. Queen made 12 tackles with 1.5 sacks. Nick Herbig and Kevin Jobity Jr. got one each, Jobity's first in the league. Cleveland went 0 for 3 in the red zone and turned it over on downs twice.

Rodgers threw an interception to Denzel Ward and we lost a fumble, so it was not a clean sheet. It was still our fourth straight win. We are 6-2, alone in first in the AFC North, and 4-0 at home under McCarthy. After the bye, it is Cincinnati on a Sunday night. Same furnace. Different fuel.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns vs Pittsburgh Steelers Week 8: Browns Fall 27-6
articles.matchup: Final: Cleveland Browns (5-3) 6, Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) 27, Sun., Nov. 1, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: at New Orleans Saints, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Caesars Superdome, New Orleans
articles.text:
Pittsburgh Steelers 27, Cleveland Browns 6. All weekend, Jurassic Quest filled the Huntington Convention Center downtown with life-size dinosaurs and a costume contest for the kids. Sunday in Pittsburgh, our offense played like one of those dinosaurs: huge, slow, and getting knocked over by a meteor every few minutes. Eight sacks. Six points. Kids, look away.

The trouble started on the opening drive. Deshaun Watson got hurt on a roughing call, Shedeur Sanders came in, and Harold Fannin Jr. had the ball stripped at our 42. Pittsburgh won the challenge. Two drives later, Patrick Queen knocked it out of Watson's hands and Pittsburgh scored five plays later. We had minus-1 yard after one quarter.

Give the defense credit for keeping it a game. Carson Schwesinger made 10 tackles, and Adin Huntington sacked Aaron Rodgers on a third-and-goal to force a field goal. Andre Szmyt hit from 32 and 49, and it was 13-6 with 45 seconds left in the half.

Then the dam broke. Pittsburgh went 69 yards in six plays, and Pat Freiermuth took a direct snap in from the 1 with one second left. Early in the third, Darnell Washington rumbled 58 yards to the 1 and Jaylen Warren scored for 27-6. Warren ran for 143 yards. We ran for 34 as a team, our lowest of the season.

Watson still threw for 324 yards, his most in a game as a Brown, going 27 of 39. Fannin caught 10 for a career-high 154 yards, the second-most ever by a Browns tight end in one game. Denzel Ward intercepted a deep throw meant for DK Metcalf in the third quarter, his third of the season, tying his career high. Corey Bojorquez dropped three punts inside the 20.

But zero for 3 in the red zone, zero for 2 on fourth down, and no touchdowns for the first time all season. We are 5-3 and the season series is split. New Orleans is next on Nov. 8. Somebody find this offense a helmet before the next meteor hits.

articles.title: Los Angeles Rams vs Los Angeles Chargers Week 8: Derby Rally 24-9
articles.matchup: Final: Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) 9, Los Angeles Rams (4-4) 24, Sun., Nov. 1, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood. Next: at Washington Commanders, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Northwest Stadium, Landover
articles.text:
Los Angeles Rams 24, Los Angeles Chargers 9, and the family is back at .500. Downtown, Grand Park's Día de los Muertos was closing out with Noche de los Muertos on Sunday afternoon, a whole city honoring the people who came before. Out in Inglewood, we spent the first half looking like we'd forgotten our own family name. Then we remembered it.

Quentin Lake did his part early, intercepting Justin Herbert and running it back 45 yards to the Chargers' 19, and Brandon McManus kicked a 30-yard field goal. That was nearly all we had for a long while. We went without a first down on our first five drives, a first in Sean McVay's career, and managed 24 yards on our first 15 plays. Cameron Dicker kicked three field goals, and we trailed 9-3.

Then the trunk of the tree held. Matthew Stafford found Tutu Atwell for 40 yards, our first first down of the day, and Kyren Williams walked in untouched from a yard out with 19 seconds left in the half. Herbert answered with a 54-yarder to Ladd McConkey down to our 1, but the clock ran out on them. We led 10-9 at halftime.

Blake Corum owned the opening drive of the second half, piling up 55 yards on eight plays and finishing it himself on a 23-yard touchdown run. Trent McDuffie intercepted Herbert and brought it back 26 yards to their 22, and two plays later Puka Nacua took a screen 18 yards for the score and a 24-9 lead. Nacua finished with 11 catches for 80 yards. Stafford went 17-of-25 for 157 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Corum ran 11 times for 73, and Williams 16 times for 56.

The defense closed it. Oronde Gadsden caught one a yard short on fourth-and-8 at our 17 with 6:39 left, and we ran 12 plays to bleed out the clock. McDuffie made nine tackles, Nate Landman eight, Josaiah Stewart got a sack and Wesley Bailey forced a strip-sack. Ethan Evans averaged 49.2 yards on five punts. We've won two of three LA derbies and back-to-back games for the first time this season, and we did it without Davante Adams. Jaylen Watson left with a shoulder injury. Super Bowls XXXIV and LVI run through this family. Washington is next.

articles.title: Los Angeles Chargers vs Los Angeles Rams Week 8: Film Room 9-24
articles.matchup: Final: Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) 9, Los Angeles Rams (4-4) 24, Sun., Nov. 1, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood. Next: vs Houston Texans, Sun., Nov. 8, 4:05 PM ET, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood
articles.text:
Los Angeles Rams 24, Los Angeles Chargers 9, and I'm taking this one straight to the film room, because I refuse to file it under that tired old phrase. On Saturday, El Segundo, where this team goes to work every week, threw its Halloween Frolic on Main Street with bounce houses, games and music. On Sunday at SoFi Stadium, we held our roommates without a first down for five straight drives and still walked out 0-7.

Clue one came early. Justin Herbert's short throw got intercepted by Quentin Lake, who brought it back 45 yards to our 19, and Brandon McManus kicked a 30-yard field goal. Cameron Dicker answered from 34, 46 and 41 yards, and Mike McDaniel dialed up back-to-back flea-flickers in the second quarter that actually worked. The Rams had 24 yards on their first 15 plays. We led 9-3.

Clue two is where the case cracks. Matthew Stafford finally found Tutu Atwell for 40 yards, the Rams' first first down of the day, and Kyren Williams walked in from a yard out with 19 seconds left in the half. Herbert hit Ladd McConkey for 54 yards down to the 1 as the clock ran out. Nine points where there should have been 16, and a 10-9 deficit at the break.

The second half opened with Blake Corum carrying the Rams 55 yards on an eight-play drive that ended with his 23-yard touchdown run. Then Trent McDuffie intercepted Herbert and ran it back 26 yards to our 22, and two plays later Puka Nacua took a screen 18 yards for 24-9. Our last real shot ended at their 17 with 6:39 left, when Oronde Gadsden caught one a yard short on fourth-and-8. The Rams ran out the clock from there.

Herbert finished 24-of-32 for 257 yards with two interceptions, and he's thrown one in all seven games. McConkey caught four for 86, Gadsden five for 52 and Quentin Johnston four for 37. The run game is the evidence nobody can explain away: 25 carries, 64 yards, with Omarion Hampton at nine for 20 and Kimani Vidal at eight for 23. Tuli Tuipulotu had a sack, and Dicker went 3-for-3. We're the only winless team left, and Derwin James went on injured reserve Saturday. Houston visits next Sunday. Back to the tape.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys vs Arizona Cardinals Week 8: A Lead Slips Away 33-30
articles.matchup: Final (OT): Arizona Cardinals (3-5) 33, Dallas Cowboys (3-5) 30, Sun., Nov. 1, AT&T Stadium, Arlington. Next: at Indianapolis Colts, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis
articles.text:
Arizona Cardinals 33, Dallas Cowboys 30 in overtime. Downtown at Levitt Pavilion, Shakespeare LIVE spent Halloween weekend staging a free Macbeth, the story of a man undone after three witches promise him everything. Across town on Sunday, the Cowboys had a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter and watched it fall apart.

I keep the business of this franchise and the football in separate boxes, and for 50 minutes the football was good. Mack Wilson Sr. stopped us on fourth-and-1 early, but the defense answered by stuffing Jeremiyah Love on fourth-and-goal at our 1. Shemar James intercepted Jacoby Brissett and returned it 33 yards, and James Mitchell recovered a fumble in the end zone for the first touchdown. Dak Prescott found Ryan Flournoy from 9. Brandon Aubrey added a field goal, and Prescott scrambled 5 yards for a 24-10 lead with 14:20 left.

The rush up front was real. Quinnen Williams had two sacks, James Houston, Von Miller and Donovan Ezeiruaku got one each, and Brissett was gone by the fourth quarter. DeMarvion Overshown forced a fumble before the half. The offense did not turn the ball over once.

Then Gardner Minshew happened. Tyler Allgeier ran 63 yards for one score and caught another. Aubrey kicked from 35 and 41 to keep us ahead 30-24, but a Rashan Gary roughing penalty extended an Arizona drive that ended in a Trey McBride touchdown. With 65 seconds left, Minshew went 80 yards in eight plays, and Michael Wilson caught the tying score with six seconds to go. Chad Ryland missed the extra point, and we still could not finish it.

In overtime, Williams sacked Minshew to start an Arizona three-and-out. Josh Sweat sacked Prescott right back. Arizona then fed Allgeier until Ryland hit a 42-yarder.

The honest part: Dallas ran 39 times for 93 yards, 2.4 per carry, and got outgained 467-261. Prescott went 19 of 29 for 195 yards and was sacked four times. CeeDee Lamb caught seven for 58. The run defense gave up 202 yards. And this is now five straight losses to Arizona, who has never lost in this building. We didn't trail until the final kick, and 3-5 is where that leaves us.

Caleb Downs left with a concussion and Jake Ferguson hurt an ankle. Next is a trip to Indianapolis.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals vs Dallas Cowboys Week 8: Minshew Steals One 33-30
articles.matchup: Final (OT): Arizona Cardinals (3-5) 33, Dallas Cowboys (3-5) 30, Sun., Nov. 1, AT&T Stadium, Arlington. Next: at Seattle Seahawks, Sun., Nov. 8, 4:25 PM ET, Lumen Field, Seattle
articles.text:
Arizona Cardinals 33, Dallas Cowboys 30 in overtime. Two nights earlier, 1,200 drones lit up the sky over State Farm Stadium for the Harry Potter DroneArt Show. On Sunday in Arlington, the Cardinals pulled off a trick nobody in our building will forget, and for three quarters it looked like there would be no magic at all.

My measuring stick is still the 2008 team that reached the Super Bowl, and the first half came nowhere near it. Jeremiyah Love got stuffed on fourth-and-goal at the Dallas 1. Shemar James intercepted Jacoby Brissett and ran it back to our 5, and Dallas fell on its own fumble in the end zone for a touchdown. Dak Prescott hit Ryan Flournoy from 9 yards. Chad Ryland's 37-yarder made it 14-3 at the half.

Brissett was sacked four times and finished 10 of 23. Then Gardner Minshew came in, and the afternoon flipped. On his first drive, Tyler Allgeier went 63 yards up the middle for a touchdown. Prescott's scramble made it 24-10, but Allgeier ripped off 52 more and caught a 5-yard score from Minshew.

Dallas kicked its way to 30-24 with Brandon Aubrey field goals, and when a Rashan Gary roughing call kept a drive alive, Minshew found Trey McBride for a 14-yard touchdown. The onside kick failed. Down six with 65 seconds left, Minshew went 80 yards in eight plays, hitting Michael Wilson for 21 and 27, then for 13 and the tying touchdown with six seconds left. Ryland pushed the extra point wide left.

He got another shot. Both teams went three-and-out to start overtime, Josh Sweat sacking Prescott on third down. Wilson ran for 17, Allgeier pounded the middle, and Ryland drilled a 42-yarder to win it.

The numbers: Minshew 17 of 23 for 188 yards, three touchdown throws and no interceptions. Allgeier ran 11 times for 147 yards and caught five for 44. Wilson caught eight for 111, McBride seven for 72. We outgained Dallas 467-261 and ran for 202 yards.

The honest part: the first half was ugly, the injuries piled up until Allgeier was the only running back we had left, with Love and Bam Knight both out and receivers Kendrick Bourne and Reggie Virgil gone too, and this team is still 3-5. That 2008 bar is a long way off. Still, it is five straight wins over Dallas and 5-0 at this stadium. Seattle is next.

articles.title: Jacksonville Jaguars vs Indianapolis Colts Week 8: Duval Rout 42-7
articles.matchup: Final: Indianapolis Colts (2-6) 7, Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) 42, Sun., Nov. 1, EverBank Stadium, Jacksonville. Next: at Baltimore Ravens, Thu., Nov. 5, 8:15 PM ET, M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore
articles.text:
Jacksonville Jaguars 42, Indianapolis Colts 7, and Duval finally got its team back. WOKV billed this as the Jaguars' first home game in more than a month, and the city warmed up Saturday afternoon with Treats at the Plaza down at Riverfront Plaza on the St. Johns. Sunday, in the rain at EverBank Stadium, the treats were all ours. We're 5-2.

Off the bye and wearing the new Bold City rivalry uniforms, we went 98 yards in 12 plays on the opening drive. Brenton Strange caught a 46-yarder, and Trevor Lawrence found Brian Thomas Jr. alone for a 12-yard touchdown. That's how you walk back into your own house.

The second quarter was the record book's kind of quarter. Bryan Thomas Jr. came up with Jonathan Taylor's fumble on a busted trick play at midfield, and rookie Nate Boerkircher scored on a 31-yard catch. Bhayshul Tuten broke three tackles on a 39-yard touchdown run. Lawrence got strip-sacked and the Colts took over at our 31, and Rayuan Lane III answered by intercepting Daniel Jones and going 92 yards with 10 seconds left. It was 28-0 at halftime.

Arik Armstead and Josh Hines-Allen split a fourth-down sack early in the third, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran 28 yards for a score. The Colts got one back, then Tuten took a screen 25 yards as the third quarter ended for 42-7. Lawrence went 10-of-14 for 210 yards and three touchdowns and watched the fourth. Tuten finished with 104 rushing yards and 55 receiving, both career highs. We ran for 183 and averaged 6.9 yards a play. Foyesade Oluokun made nine tackles and a sack, and Branson Combs added an interception.

Now the splits, because they matter. That's 12 straight home wins over the Colts, who last won here in 2014. It's seven straight regular-season home wins, and we've outscored those visitors 271-75. The three-game AFC South lead puts us in a spot this franchise hasn't seen since 1999. The cost was DaVon Hamilton, who left with what looked like a season-ending knee injury. Baltimore comes up fast on Thursday night.

articles.title: Indianapolis Colts vs Jacksonville Jaguars Week 8: Smashed 7-42
articles.matchup: Final: Indianapolis Colts (2-6) 7, Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) 42, Sun., Nov. 1, EverBank Stadium, Jacksonville. Next: vs Dallas Cowboys, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis
articles.text:
Jacksonville Jaguars 42, Indianapolis Colts 7, and I've been counting this franchise's history since the Baltimore days, so believe me when I say this one goes near the bottom of the pile. Back home, the Indianapolis Zoo had its elephants scheduled to stomp giant pumpkins at 4:30 Sunday afternoon to close out ZooBoo. Down in Jacksonville, in the rain, we got stomped first. We're 2-6.

The tone got set on the opening possession. The Jaguars went 98 yards in 12 plays, with Brenton Strange grabbing a 46-yarder along the way and Brian Thomas Jr. catching a 12-yard touchdown from Trevor Lawrence. We trailed 7-0 after one quarter, and that was the last time this game felt close.

The second quarter is the one I'll be counting for years. A trick play went wrong, Jonathan Taylor lost the ball, and Jacksonville took over at midfield. Rookie Nate Boerkircher scored from 31 yards out. Bhayshul Tuten broke three tackles on a 39-yard touchdown run. Then we finally caught a break when Jaylahn Tuimoloau strip-sacked Lawrence and we took over at the Jacksonville 31. Then Rayuan Lane III intercepted Daniel Jones and ran it back 92 yards with 10 seconds left in the half. It was 28-0 at the break.

Jacksonville sacked Jones on fourth down early in the third, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran 28 yards for another score. Our only points came on Jones' 6-yard touchdown throw to Josh Downs, making it 35-7, before Tuten took a screen 25 yards to end the quarter at 42-7. Jones finished 19-of-28 for 144 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, and Anthony Richardson replaced him in the fourth. Taylor managed 23 yards on eight carries. Keenan Allen caught seven balls for 67 yards, and DJ Giddens ran six times for 43.

CJ Allen made 10 tackles and a sack, and Laiatu Latu dropped Lawrence for a 15-yard loss. Seth McGowan returned four kickoffs for 103 yards. The rest was nine penalties, 3-of-11 on third down and 0-for-2 on fourth, five days after we traded DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson. We haven't won in Jacksonville since 2014, and we've lost four straight. This franchise owns the 1958 title and Super Bowls V and XLI. Dallas comes to Lucas Oil next Sunday, and the count begins again.

articles.title: Detroit Lions vs Minnesota Vikings Week 8: Lions Hand Vikings First Loss, 19-15
articles.matchup: Final: Minnesota Vikings (6-1) 15, Detroit Lions (5-2) 19, Sun., Nov. 1, Ford Field, Detroit. Next: at Miami Dolphins, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Detroit Lions 19, Minnesota Vikings 15. On Sunday afternoon the Detroit Riverfront hosted its Día de los Muertos celebration at Robert C. Valade Park, with ballet folklórico, Mariachi Mexico de Detroit and a community ofrenda by the water. Up at Ford Field, Detroit Lions vs Minnesota Vikings turned into a four-quarter street fight, and the Vikings walked out with their first loss of the season.

It did not start clean. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams drew taunting flags on our first two drives, and a touchdown grab by St. Brown got overturned on review. Jake Bates bailed us out from 25 yards. Kyler Murray answered early in the second quarter with a 1-yard touchdown throw to Justin Jefferson, and Andrew Van Ginkel spent the half chasing Jared Goff around the pocket.

Then D.J. Reed dove in front of Jordan Addison for an interception late in the half, and Bates drilled a 37-yarder with two seconds left. Vikings 7, Lions 6 at the break, and our running game had barely cleared its throat.

The second half belonged to the backs. Jahmyr Gibbs ripped off a 30-yard touchdown run late in the third for a 12-7 lead. It was his 10th touchdown of the season, and only Gibbs and Barry Sanders have reached 10 in four straight seasons for this franchise. Murray fought back with an 8-yard touchdown to T.J. Hockenson and a two-point throw to Addison, and Minnesota led 15-12 with 8:44 to go.

So we ran it right at them. Gibbs for 17. Sione Vaki for 5, 12 and 10. Gibbs for 9, then 9 more. Goff found Williams in the back of the end zone from 7 yards with 4:35 left, the defense forced a three-and-out, and we ran out the clock.

We finished with 230 rushing yards, 164 of them after halftime. Gibbs had 153 on 23 carries and Vaki 65 on 11. Goff went 18 of 25 for 176 yards and his first interception of the season, and he has now thrown a touchdown in 29 straight games. The defense allowed 266 yards and 15 points, our fewest all season, and Minnesota went 3 of 10 on third down.

Nobody partied, though. Jack Campbell was carted off in the fourth quarter and taken to a hospital with a neck injury. Detroit is praying for him tonight.

Three straight wins, 5-2, unbeaten in the division, and Miami is next on Nov. 8. This window does not stay open forever. Today we kicked it wider.

articles.matchup: Final: Minnesota Vikings (6-1) 15, Detroit Lions (5-2) 19, Sun., Nov. 1, Ford Field, Detroit. Next: vs. Buffalo Bills, Mon., Nov. 9, 8:15 PM ET, U.S. Bank Stadium, Minneapolis
articles.text:
Detroit Lions 19, Minnesota Vikings 15. I spent six weeks telling everyone that 6-0 was a rumor, and on Sunday at Ford Field, Minnesota Vikings vs Detroit Lions proved me right in the worst way. Back home, the BareBones Halloween Extravaganza was set for its final night in Powderhorn Park, a puppet show about the cycles of living and dying. Fitting. The undefeated part of our season just finished its cycle.

For a half, the purple held. Detroit drew two taunting flags on its first two drives and lost a touchdown to replay. Kyler Murray lofted a 1-yard throw early in the second quarter, and Justin Jefferson caught it for a 7-3 lead. Andrew Van Ginkel was a menace, with a career-high 2.5 sacks. D.J. Reed's diving interception in front of Jordan Addison set up a Detroit field goal right before the half, and we still went in up 7-6.

Then the ground gave way. Detroit ran for 66 yards in the first half and 164 in the second. Jahmyr Gibbs went 30 yards for a touchdown late in the third. Murray answered with the drive of the day, an 8-yard touchdown to T.J. Hockenson and a two-point throw to Addison, and we led 15-12 with 8:44 left.

We held that lead for a little over four minutes. Detroit ran six straight times, Gibbs and Sione Vaki taking turns, and Jared Goff hit Jameson Williams from 7 yards with 4:35 left. Our offense went three-and-out, Kevin O'Connell chose to punt on fourth-and-5 from our 33, and we never saw the ball again.

Murray went 17 of 29 for 210 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, and he ran for 35. Addison caught three balls for 66, including a 51-yarder. Hockenson had four for 58, and Jefferson had five for 33. We ran for 81 yards and went 3 of 10 on third down, and Detroit held the ball for 35:43. Joshua Metellus made 13 tackles, Eric Wilson had 11 and a sack, and Byron Murphy Jr. and Blake Cashman made 10 apiece.

Our whole section went quiet when Jack Campbell was carted off in the fourth quarter. Some things matter more than a division game.

We are 6-1 and still first in the NFC North. The last loss before this one came on Nov. 30, 2025, at Seattle. Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on Monday night, Nov. 9, and we get an extra day to get ready. I will not panic in November. I will not celebrate in it, either.

articles.title: Cincinnati Bengals vs Tennessee Titans Week 8: Burrow Ends It 43-36
articles.matchup: Final (OT): Tennessee Titans (1-7) 36, Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) 43, Sun., Nov. 1, Paycor Stadium, Cincinnati. Next: at Atlanta Falcons, Sun., Nov. 8, 9:30 AM ET, Santiago Bernabéu, Madrid
articles.text:
Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36 in overtime. While the Cincinnati Zoo ran HallZOOween on Sunday afternoon, the crowd at Paycor Stadium got a Halloween scare of its own, and it started early.

Every question with this team is a quarterback question, and for one quarter the answer was ugly. Joe Burrow threw deep for Ja'Marr Chase and Amani Hooker intercepted it at the Tennessee 9. Tony Pollard went 40 yards for a touchdown. Joey Slye kicked two field goals. It was 13-0 Titans after the first quarter.

Then Burrow went to work. A holding call wiped out a Chase Brown touchdown, so on third-and-18 he put it on Chase from 30 yards out. DJ Turner forced a Wan'Dale Robinson fumble that Josh Newton recovered, and Burrow hit Jack Endries from 1 yard with 20 seconds left in the half for a 14-13 lead. Hooker picked Burrow off again on the first drive of the third quarter, but Boye Mafe answered with a strip-sack of Cam Ward, Dexter Lawrence II recovered, and on the next snap Tee Higgins caught a 17-yard touchdown.

It was never comfortable. Hooker intercepted Burrow once more, three in all. Tennessee tied it 21-21, Demetrius Knight Jr. and Lawrence dropped Pollard in the end zone for a safety, and the fourth quarter brought three lead changes and a tie. Mike Gesicki's 25-yard touchdown made it 29-28, his fifth straight game with a score. Ward answered with a touchdown and a two-point throw for 36-29.

So there it was, 3:46 left, down seven. Burrow drove us down and found Higgins from 18 yards with 1:17 to go, and Lawrence sacked Ward with 32 seconds left in regulation to force a punt. We got the ball first in overtime, and Burrow finished a five-play, 70-yard drive by scrambling nine yards into the end zone himself. The defense closed it with a fourth-down stop on the final Tennessee snap.

The numbers: Burrow 38 of 48 for 462 yards, five touchdown throws and the winning run. Higgins caught 10 for 155 and two scores, Chase 11 for 141, and the offense went 7 of 10 on third down. The honest part: three interceptions, a Brown fumble that led to a Titans score, and 440 yards allowed to a 1-7 team. That has to get cleaned up.

Three straight wins and 5-2 for the first time since 2021. Next stop is Madrid against Atlanta.

articles.matchup: Final (OT): Tennessee Titans (1-7) 36, Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) 43, Sun., Nov. 1, Paycor Stadium, Cincinnati. Next: bye week, then Jacksonville Jaguars, Sun., Nov. 15, 1:00 PM ET, Nissan Stadium, Nashville
articles.text:
Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36 in overtime. On Halloween night the Five Points corner of East Nashville filled up for All Hallows East, costumes and live music until 10. The next afternoon, the Titans walked into Paycor Stadium and gave Cincinnati a first quarter to remember for all the wrong reasons.

I grade this season on growth, and Sunday gave me a lot of it before it gave me the loss. Joey Slye hit from 46. Tony Pollard broke a 40-yard touchdown run. Amani Hooker read Joe Burrow deep for Ja'Marr Chase and intercepted it at our 9, and Slye added a 29-yarder. It was 13-0 after one quarter.

Hooker was not finished. He intercepted Burrow again on the opening drive of the third quarter and a third time at our 5 late in that quarter. That made him the first Titan with three interceptions in a game since Kevin Byard in 2016. Jacob Martin added three sacks, including a 15-yard loss on fourth-and-2 at our 5 before the half. Anthony Hill Jr. made 14 tackles.

Then there is Cam Ward. He went 26 of 40 for 304 yards, two touchdown throws and no interceptions, the first 300-yard game of his career. After a Boye Mafe strip-sack put us behind, Ward led an 80-yard answer, Pollard scored from the 1 and Ward ran in the two-point try himself for a 21-21 tie. When Alontae Taylor punched the ball away from Chase Brown, Ward hit Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score and a 28-23 lead. Down 29-28 late, he found Gunnar Helm for 25 on third down, then Wan'Dale Robinson for 15 and a touchdown, then Helm for two. 36-29 with 3:46 to go.

The honest part is the end. Burrow found Tee Higgins from 18 yards with 1:17 left. Cincinnati got the ball first in overtime and went 70 yards in five plays, Burrow running the last nine himself. Our answer died on fourth-and-3 at our 35 with a throw to Elic Ayomanor that fell incomplete. The defense gave up 510 yards, and a safety on Pollard in our own end zone cost two points we needed.

Pollard ran 21 times for 117 yards and two scores. Dike caught five for 71 and returned six kickoffs for 160. Tennessee is 1-7, which hurts. The kid looked like a franchise quarterback for four quarters, which counts.

The bye comes at the right time. Jacksonville visits Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15.

articles.title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs Atlanta Falcons Week 8: Mud Run 16-0
articles.matchup: Final: Atlanta Falcons (3-5) 0, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) 16, Sun., Nov. 1, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: at Chicago Bears, Sun., Nov. 8, 8:20 PM ET, Soldier Field, Chicago
articles.text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers 16, Atlanta Falcons 0, and we own this one from the first handoff to the last. Busch Gardens closed out Howl-O-Scream on Saturday night, but the real scare in this town came Sunday afternoon in driving rain at Raymond James Stadium. It belonged to Atlanta. We're 3-5, and we've won three of four since that 0-4 hole.

The Falcons blinked first when Nick Folk pushed a 53-yarder wide left on their opening drive. Chase McLaughlin made them pay with field goals of 46 and 34 yards in the first quarter and 42 in the second, and he's now 19 for 19 this season. We should have had more. Alex Anzalone intercepted Michael Penix Jr., a roughness flag set us up at the Atlanta 18, and then Bucky Irving lost the ball at the 1 out of the end zone. That one's on us, and we own it.

Then the ground game took the deed to the place. Baker Mayfield, in his second game back from a fractured thumb, handed off 52 times. We ran it 56 times for 324 yards, a franchise record, topping the 283 we put up at Philadelphia in 2015. Irving carried 27 times for 170 yards and scored on a 4-yard run late in the third quarter for the 16-0 cushion. Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25 carries, then ran it seven straight times at the end to close the door. Mayfield went 0-for-3 through the air. No team had gone a full game without a completion since Buffalo in 1974.

The defense owned the rest. Penix went 8-of-24 with four interceptions: two from Anzalone, one from Zyon McCollum and one from Jacob Parrish on fourth-and-6 at our 32. Parrish and Antoine Winfield Jr. each made seven tackles. Atlanta went 0-for-12 on third down. Jahan Dotson got loose for 76 yards in the fourth quarter, and we held at the 14 anyway on fourth-and-2.

Riley Dixon punted six times for a 44.8 average and kept the field tilted all day. The one gut punch was Yaya Diaby leaving with a knee injury in the first quarter. We sit a half-game behind Carolina in the NFC South, and next comes Chicago at Soldier Field on Sunday night. Bring the rain gear again.

articles.title: Atlanta Falcons vs Tampa Bay Buccaneers Week 8: Blanked 0-16
articles.matchup: Final: Atlanta Falcons (3-5) 0, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) 16, Sun., Nov. 1, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: vs Cincinnati Bengals, Sun., Nov. 8, 9:30 AM ET, Santiago Bernabéu, Madrid
articles.text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers 16, Atlanta Falcons 0, and the NFC South race got a little harder to watch from where we sit. On Saturday, Mercedes-Benz Stadium was packed for Georgia's win over Florida, our building rocking with somebody else's noise. On Sunday, we went south into a Tampa downpour and never put a single point on the board. We're 3-5, level with the Bucs, and every division game we drop like this one costs double.

It went sideways early. Nick Folk's 53-yard try on our opening drive drifted wide left, and Chase McLaughlin answered with field goals from 46 and 34 yards in the first quarter and 42 more in the second. Down 9-0, we caught one break when Jessie Bates punched the ball loose from Bucky Irving at our 1 and it bounced out of the end zone for a touchback. That trip only happened because Alex Anzalone intercepted Michael Penix Jr. and a 15-yard unnecessary roughness flag on Drake London handed Tampa the ball at our 18. Then Bijan Robinson got stuffed on fourth-and-1 at their 36 with 1:30 left in the half.

Tampa barely threw. Baker Mayfield went 0-for-3, and the Bucs simply ran it at us 56 times for 324 yards. Irving had 170 and the only touchdown, a 4-yard run late in the third quarter, and Kenny Gainwell added 140. Kendal Daniels made 13 tackles, Xavier Watts made nine, and Harold Perkins Jr. got a sack, but we never got them off the field long enough.

Our offense is the part that stings. Penix finished 8-of-24 for 125 yards with four interceptions, two by Anzalone. We went 0-for-12 on third down with eight first downs and 224 yards. Robinson ran 19 times for 76, and London caught one ball for 8 yards on six targets. The best shot came in the fourth quarter, when Jahan Dotson hauled in a 76-yarder from our own 2 to the Tampa 22. That drive died at the 14 on a fourth-and-2 throw to Olamide Zaccheaus that fell incomplete.

Jake Bailey punted four times for a 48.3 average, which tells you plenty. Zachariah Branch and Samson Ebukam both left with hamstring injuries. Next up is Cincinnati in Madrid at the Santiago Bernabéu, with us as the home team. The NFC South doesn't care what country we play in. We need that one.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills vs Baltimore Ravens Week 8: Bills Bury Baltimore 36-10
articles.matchup: Final: Baltimore Ravens (4-4) 10, Buffalo Bills (6-1) 36, Sun., Nov. 1, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park. Next: at Minnesota Vikings, Mon., Nov. 9, 8:15 PM ET, U.S. Bank Stadium, Minneapolis
articles.text:
Buffalo Bills 36, Baltimore Ravens 10. Across town on Sunday, the Scarecrow Trail at the Buffalo Botanical Gardens had dozens of straw figures and ghosts tucked among the mums. In Orchard Park, the Baltimore offense looked about as dangerous as any of them by the fourth quarter.

I don't hand out trophies for October. I judge this team by January, and what matters from this one is how it got done. The first drive told you plenty: Josh Allen kept the ball on fourth-and-goal from the 1 and walked in. Tyler Bass followed with a 56-yard field goal, and it was 10-0 before most of the stadium sat down.

Allen gave one back, an interception at our own 17 that turned into a Derrick Henry score, and it sat at 10-7 for too long. The defense took over from there. Cole Bishop sacked Tyler Huntley and forced a fumble that Kaleb Elarms-Orr pounced on. Davison Igbinosun intercepted rookie Joe Fagnano. Tyler Bass turned both gifts into points, the second from 51 yards with nine seconds left in the half. He went 3 for 3 and now has 21 straight makes, a franchise record.

The second half was Allen with the ball and receivers running free. A 49-yard strike to DJ Moore set up James Cook's 5-yard run. A 40-yard catch by Dalton Kincaid set up Moore's 11-yard touchdown. Then Allen found Kincaid for 23 yards and the 36-10 final. Allen finished 21 of 34 for 289 yards, two touchdown throws and a rushing score. Cook carried 21 times for 80 yards, and Khalil Shakir caught five for 64.

Baltimore got 144 yards all day. Landon Jackson, Greg Rousseau, Bishop and TJ Parker each got a sack, and the Ravens went 3 of 13 on third down.

Now the honest part, because January doesn't care about the scoreboard in Week 8. Ten penalties for 87 yards is sloppy. Moore lost a fumble at the Baltimore 18 when Roquan Smith ripped it out. The Allen interception was a bad read. Joshua Palmer left with a hamstring injury. Against a Ravens team down to its third quarterback, none of it cost us. In a playoff game it would.

Still, 6-1 is 6-1, and the Bills went 4 of 5 on fourth down. Next is a Monday night trip to Minnesota.

articles.title: Baltimore Ravens vs Buffalo Bills Week 8: Three QBs, One Rout 36-10
articles.matchup: Final: Baltimore Ravens (4-4) 10, Buffalo Bills (6-1) 36, Sun., Nov. 1, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park. Next: Jacksonville Jaguars, Thu., Nov. 5, 8:15 PM ET, M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore
articles.text:
Buffalo Bills 36, Baltimore Ravens 10. Back home on Sunday morning, families hauled their old jack-o'-lanterns up to the roof of the Maryland Science Center for the Pumpkin Smash and sent them flying for compost. By late afternoon in Orchard Park, the whole season felt like it had been tossed off a roof with them.

It went wrong on the first snap. Lamar Jackson's throwing hand hit Greg Rousseau's arm on an incomplete throw, he hurt his right thumb, and he did not come back. Tyler Huntley came in, got sacked by Cole Bishop, lost the ball, which Buffalo recovered at our 20, and limped off with a toe injury. That handed the game to Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie from UConn making his NFL debut on the road in Buffalo.

Give the kid credit for standing in there. He went 10 of 21 for 91 yards with an interception, and nobody expected more. Josh Allen's 1-yard keeper on fourth-and-goal opened the scoring, Tyler Bass hit from 56, and Broderick Washington Jr. intercepted Allen at the Buffalo 17 to give Derrick Henry a 2-yard score. At 10-7 we were breathing.

Then the mistakes stacked up. Davison Igbinosun intercepted Fagnano late in the half and Bass drilled a 51-yarder with nine seconds left. Tyler Loop clanged a 34-yarder off the left upright. Henry ran one in from 10 in the third quarter and Ronnie Stanley's holding flag erased it. Loop's 26-yarder made it 16-10, and that was the last time this felt like a game.

The honest part: 144 yards of offense, 10 first downs, 3 of 13 on third down, three turnovers and four sacks taken. Buffalo kept the ball for more than 37 minutes. The defense I always judge first held up for a half and then wore down, giving up 426 yards by the end.

There were still Ravens worth naming. Roquan Smith made 11 tackles and punched the ball loose from DJ Moore. Malaki Starks added 10 tackles. Rasheen Ali brought back five kickoffs for 147 yards, one for 59. Henry's touchdown was the 136th of his career from scrimmage, tying Marshall Faulk for fourth all time.

That is three losses in a row, and the Jaguars come to M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday night with four days to get a quarterback healthy. Baltimore has to find one fast.

articles.title: New York Jets vs Raiders Week 8: Late Rally Sinks Jets 38-33
articles.matchup: Final: Raiders (4-4) 38, New York Jets (2-6) 33, Sun., Nov. 1, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford. Next: at Kansas City Chiefs, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City
articles.text:
Raiders 38, New York Jets 33. Sunday morning, on the 50th anniversary of the five-borough course, Sweden's Andreas Almgren ran his first marathon ever and won the New York City Marathon, pulling away in Central Park to win by 13 seconds. A few hours later at MetLife Stadium, the Jets ran the first half like Almgren and lost the race by five points.

And what a first half. We scored on our first six possessions for the first time since 2008. Garrett Wilson caught a 31-yarder on the first play, and Jason Sanders kicked field goals from 21 and 36. Geno Smith threw 18 yards to Isaiah Williams for a 13-7 lead.

Then Dylan Laube, a kid from Westhampton, took the kickoff back 95 yards. We answered anyway. Smith found Adonai Mitchell for a 12-yard touchdown and 20-14, and Sanders hit a 39-yarder with nine seconds left. Under Aaron Glenn the Jets had been outscored 107-6 in the final two minutes of first halves, and those were our first points in that window this season. Jets 23, Raiders 14 at the half.

Braelon Allen ran 21 yards around the left end for 30-21 in the third, part of a career-high 147 yards on 21 carries. Mitchell finished with seven catches for a career-high 142. We outgained the Raiders 439 yards to 333.

Everybody says yards do not win games. I hate when everybody is right. Kirk Cousins sneaked in from the 1, we punted for the first time all day late in the third, Ashton Jeanty turned a short throw into 45 yards, and Jalen Nailor caught a 2-yard touchdown for 35-30 with 11:33 left. Smith hit Mitchell for 47 to get us inside the 20, we stalled at the 13, and Sanders made it 35-33 with his fourth field goal.

The Raiders ran the clock down, and Matt Gay hit from 53. Smith's last throw to the end zone was intercepted by Jeremy Chinn.

Smith went 20 of 32 for 290 yards, two touchdowns and that interception. Wilson caught six for 83. Jamien Sherwood made 14 tackles, and Will McDonald IV sacked Cousins once. We were 2 of 6 in the red zone, and that is the game in one number.

Three straight losses, and we are 2-6. Next Sunday we go to Arrowhead to face Kansas City, and every expert alive already knows how that ends. Experts knew how Super Bowl III ended, too.

articles.text:

I judge a game by who is standing across from us, and I did not circle the Jets. I was wrong. They scored on their first six possessions. Kirk Cousins answered the opening field goal with a 12-yard touchdown throw to Brock Bowers, but New York came right back with a field goal and an 18-yard Geno Smith touchdown to Isaiah Williams.

Then Dylan Laube took the next kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown and a 14-13 lead. It was the first kickoff-return touchdown in the NFL this season and the Raiders' first since Jacoby Ford in 2011. Laube grew up in Westhampton, New York, and he picked the Jets to do it against.

The rest of the half went to New York. Smith hit Adonai Mitchell for a 12-yard touchdown, Connor Heyward got stuffed on a fourth-down tush push, and Jason Sanders kicked a 39-yarder with nine seconds left. Down 23-14 at halftime, with Braelon Allen already at 121 rushing yards.

Cousins came out firing. Bowers caught a 2-yard touchdown to make it 23-21. Allen ran 21 yards for 30-21, and Cousins answered with a 1-yard sneak, his first rushing touchdown of the year. It was Nailor's first touchdown as a Raider.

Sanders cut it to 35-33 with his fourth field goal. We ground down the clock, Matt Gay drilled a 53-yarder, and Jeremy Chinn got both feet down in the end zone to intercept Smith's last heave.

We went 4 for 4 in the red zone.

articles.matchup: Final: New England Patriots (5-3) 24, Miami Dolphins (1-6) 19, Sun., Nov. 1, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens. Next: vs Detroit Lions, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
New England Patriots 24, Miami Dolphins 19, and Biscayne Bay has company. On Saturday, Red Bull Flugtag teams launched homemade flying machines off a deck at Bayfront Park and splashed into the water. On Sunday, in a steady rain at Hard Rock Stadium, our guys built something that flew beautifully for a half before it hit the drink.

Gordon ran 19 times for 69, Washington caught five for 40, Greg Dulcich four for 43, and Coleman three for 46. Jordyn Brooks made 11 tackles, and Josh Uche added a sack. articles.matchup: Final: New England Patriots (5-3) 24, Miami Dolphins (1-6) 19, Sun., Nov. 1, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens. Next: vs Green Bay Packers, Sun., Nov. 8, 4:25 PM ET, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough
articles.text:
New England Patriots 24, Miami Dolphins 19, and I'll take a soaked jersey every week if it ends like this. Salem closed out Haunted Happenings on Halloween night with a drone show over the North River. On Sunday our guys flew south into a downpour at Hard Rock Stadium and spent a half looking like they'd stayed up for it.

The first half was ugly. Andy Borregales opened with a 34-yard field goal, but Jacob Rodriguez punched the ball loose from Efton Chism and Miami turned it into three. Zane Gonzalez banked a 52-yarder off the left upright, Borregales missed from 40, and Malik Willis drove Miami 70 yards in 11 plays for Malik Washington's 1-yard touchdown catch with eight seconds left. We trailed 13-3 and got sacked twice by Chop Robinson along the way.

Then Drake Maye found his feet in the wet. Mike Vrabel threw the red flag on a ruled incompletion, and the replay gave Kyle Williams a 43-yard touchdown. Next came a 13-play, 73-yard grind, kept alive when replay upheld DeMario Douglas on fourth down, and Maye faked the pitch and ran it in from 2 for a 17-13 lead. Maye completed his first eight throws of the half.

Kevin Byard sealed the swing early in the fourth. Willis's throw caromed off DaQuan Jones, and Byard grabbed his first interception as a Patriot. One play later, Maye hit Douglas deep for a 48-yard touchdown and 24-13. Gonzalez missed from 43, rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. scored from 35 with 2:04 left, the two-point try failed, and Rhamondre Stevenson pulled in the onside kick. Kneel, kneel, ballgame.

Maye went 16-of-20 for 199 yards and two touchdowns, ran for another, and has accounted for at least three touchdowns in five straight games. Stevenson ran 19 times for 82, and Douglas caught three for 76. The defense sacked Willis five times, with Cory Durden and Gabe Jacas getting a sack and a half each, and Christian Elliss made nine tackles. We were down 13-3 and won without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson. Green Bay is next at Gillette. Six banners hang in Foxborough for a reason.

articles.title: Denver Broncos vs Kansas City Chiefs Week 8: Mile High Stand 28-24
articles.matchup: Final: Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) 24, Denver Broncos (6-2) 28, Sun., Nov. 1, Empower Field at Mile High, Denver. Next: at Carolina Panthers, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Bank of America Stadium, Charlotte
articles.text:
Denver Broncos 28, Kansas City Chiefs 24, and we're sitting alone atop the AFC West. Across town, the Denver Coliseum spent Sunday on its Día de Muertos Festival, a community altar, folkloric dancing and music from 11 in the morning until 8 at night. At Empower Field at Mile High, 76,831 of us watched this team claw back from a grave of its own.

Wil Lutz opened with field goals from 39 and 45, but Patrick Mahomes hit Rashee Rice for a score and then rookie Emmett Johnson for 73 yards from their own 5. The second quarter's best moment was ours, though. Bo Nix and the offense got stuffed at the Kansas City 1 on three straight snaps, and on fourth down Nix found Jaylen Waddle for the touchdown. Harrison Butker's 45-yarder after a 38-yard Johnson catch made it 17-13 at the half.

The third quarter tested every one of us. Three straight three-and-outs, boos raining down, and Noah Gray's 4-yard touchdown catch made it 24-13. Mile High doesn't quit at 5,280 feet, and neither did Nix.

Nix took us 80 yards in nine plays, Marvin Mims Jr. ripped off a 14-yard run to the 4, and Nate Adkins caught the touchdown before Nix hit Waddle for two. Singleton sacked Mahomes on the next drive, Butker missed from 54, and Nix fired a strike to Jonah Coleman for 51 yards. Coleman punched it in from the 5 with 1:56 left. Then the stand. Kansas City reached our 1 with 35 seconds left. JL Skinner stuffed Kenneth Walker III, the Chiefs got flagged for a false start, and Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes as time ran out.

Nix finished 20-of-32 for 222 yards, two touchdowns and no turnovers. Coleman ran 11 times for 41 and caught four for 63, and Courtland Sutton grabbed four for 53. Alex Singleton made 14 tackles, Pat Surtain II had eight and Zach Allen hit Mahomes three times. We went 3-for-3 in the red zone. Sean Payton is now unbeaten at home against Kansas City, and Carolina is next. Orange crush forever.

articles.matchup: Final: Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) 24, Denver Broncos (6-2) 28, Sun., Nov. 1, Empower Field at Mile High, Denver. Next: vs New York Jets, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City
articles.text:
Denver Broncos 28, Kansas City Chiefs 24, and I'm still staring at the ceiling. On Halloween night, the West Bottoms threw a free party on the Rock Island Bridge, music and costumes for all ages. Twenty-four hours later, we went up to Mile High looking to sweep the team we handled at Arrowhead in Week 1. Patrick Mahomes gave us every reason to believe.

Wil Lutz kicked two early field goals, but Mahomes hit Rashee Rice for an 11-yard score, and then came the throw of the day. Pinned at our own 5, Mahomes found rookie Emmett Johnson for a 73-yard touchdown and a 14-6 lead. Denver got stuffed at our 1 three straight times before Bo Nix hit Jaylen Waddle on fourth down, but Johnson's 38-yard catch set up Harrison Butker's 45-yarder. We led 17-13 at the half.

The third quarter was pure Andy Reid. Denver went three-and-out on its first three drives, the home crowd booed, and Mahomes marched us 63 yards in 11 plays, finishing with a 4-yard throw to Noah Gray. That's 24-13, and you could hear Mile High go quiet.

Then it slipped. Nix led an 80-yard, nine-play drive, found Nate Adkins for the score and hit Waddle on the two-point try. Our answer stalled when Alex Singleton sacked Mahomes, and Butker's 54-yard try sailed wide right with 2:36 left. One snap later Nix hit Jonah Coleman for 51 yards, and Coleman ran it in from the 5. Johnson ripped off a 44-yard kickoff return, Travis Kelce caught a 32-yarder, and Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl LX MVP with Seattle, got us to the 1 with 35 seconds left. An incompletion. Walker stuffed by JL Skinner. A false start. Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes as time ran out.

Mahomes went 30-of-41 for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Johnson caught five for 128, Rice seven for 53, Kelce five for 67, and Walker ran 21 times for 69. Nick Bolton made nine tackles and George Karlaftis had a strip-sack. Eleven penalties for 105 yards is the stat I can't shake. That's two straight losses and second place in the AFC West. The Jets come to Arrowhead next Sunday. Chiefs Kingdom rides on.

articles.matchup: Final: Washington Commanders (2-4-1) 27, Philadelphia Eagles (2-6) 10, Sun., Nov. 1, Northwest Stadium, Landover. Next: vs Los Angeles Rams, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Northwest Stadium, Landover
articles.text:
Washington Commanders 27, Philadelphia Eagles 10, and the whole DMV can dance tonight. The Washington Ballet opened its 50th season this weekend with Go-Go 50 at the Warner Theatre, ballet set to the heartbeat of D.C. On Sunday Night Football in Landover, our guys found the beat after a rough first quarter and never let Philadelphia score again.

That start was ugly. Drew Stevens missed from 55, Andrew Mukuba forced a Chig Okonkwo fumble that Zack Baun recovered, and Saquon Barkley took a direct snap in from 3. Philly led 10-0. Then Stevens buried a 56-yarder with 28 seconds left in the quarter, and the comeback had its first note.

Jayden Daniels went to work in the second quarter: 11 plays, 89 yards, Treylon Burks grabbing 21 along the way, and an 8-yard touchdown throw to Stefon Diggs to tie it 10-10. Daniels took a hard hit on the last drive of the half and got up slow, but he stayed in, Diggs grabbed a 20-yarder on that drive, and Stevens banked a 39-yarder for 13-10.

The defense did the rest. Dorance Armstrong stripped Tanner McKee late in the third, Charles Omenihu recovered, and Daniels dropped a 53-yard dime to Burks to set up Stevens from 25. Jake Elliott's 41-yard retry hit the left upright after a Philly illegal formation flag wiped out his make. Stevens hit from 42 for 19-10, Rasul Douglas intercepted McKee on fourth-and-25, and Rachaad White ripped off 33 yards before punching it in from 1. Austin Ekeler ran in the two-point try. Twenty-seven straight points.

Daniels went 16-of-29 for 217 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions, his first win as a starter since he beat the Chargers on Oct. 5, 2025. Burks caught three for 81, Antonio Williams five for 54, and White ran for 55. Stevens went 4-of-5 for 13 points. Five different guys sacked McKee: Armstrong, Omenihu, Shy Tuttle, K'Lavon Chaisson and Odafe Oweh. Nick Cross made nine tackles. We did it without Terry McLaurin, too. At 2-4-1 we're still in the NFC East hunt, and the Rams come to Northwest Stadium next Sunday. Hail to the Commanders.

Jake Elliott's 36-yard make was wiped out by an illegal formation flag, and his 41-yard retry hit the left upright.
McKee was sacked five times and intercepted once; the Eagles have lost six straight.
Ten points in the first quarter, then the gloves came off the wrong guys.
